_schema: LEGEND benchmark · input surface spec v1
_note: The allowlist. `benchmark_input_surface.py` copies exactly what is listed here and
nothing else, and `verify` refuses a surface holding anything not listed. Source paths
are relative to --source-root, which is the LEGEND root checkout: the packet lives under
files/, which is git-ignored, so it exists in a checkout and never in a commit.
Adding a path here is a governed change to a tracked artifact, reviewable as such.
Removed on purpose and recorded so the omission is not read as an oversight: the
page renders and figure crops under *_assets/ (S_fig_*, S_page_*, S_native_*, figs/*,
S10_caption_*). They are renders of the source, and their SELECTION encodes a prior
reader's attention — which pages, which panels, at which dpi. Each reader renders what
it needs from the PDF and declares its renders as figure artifacts with digests.
_expected_output_note: The EXACT set of paths a reader is told to write, and the only paths --post-read
exempts from the content scan and the allowlist check.
Revision 2, Mirror finding B-4. The exemption used to be 'anything under an output
slot', which is far wider than the blind spot it was written for. The blind spot is
ONE path: the reader's own work manifest lands where LEGEND's prior manifest lives,
because deepdive_manifest.py derives that path from disease and PMID and cannot put
it elsewhere. Six other forbidden paths sit under the same two slots, collide with
nothing the reader was asked to write, and were being skipped along with it.
The tool COMPUTES the blind spot as the intersection of this list with
forbidden_prior_output_paths, and prints it on every --post-read run. It is size 1.
A path added here that collides with a forbidden path therefore widens a printed
blind spot; it cannot widen a silent one.
Revision 3, Mirror finding M-2. That last sentence was true of THIS key and false of
the exemption, because the exemption is spread over this key AND
expected_output_prefixes, and the census read only this one. See
_expected_output_prefix_note. What --post-read leaves unchecked is now enumerated
from the tree on every run, under [UNCHECKED], and the blind spot is one of three
populations rather than the whole of it.
_expected_output_prefix_note: Renders cannot be enumerated in advance: the reader chooses which panels to render.
So this is a prefix, and a prefix is the one place where the tool admits a path it
was never shown. Revision 2 admitted ANY path under it, which made a decodable text
file at output/renders/smuggled.md exempt from both the allowlist check and the
identifier scan — the same bytes at a non-exempt path produced two findings.
The exemption is written on BYTES, not on position: a file under one of these
prefixes is an expected output only when the tool CANNOT decode it as UTF-8 text. A
render is pixels, and pixels are what the scan cannot read. A decodable file here is
exempt from nothing, is reported by the allowlist check and the scan, and is
classified UNEXPECTED by freeze. BENCHMARK_INSTRUCTIONS section 1 tells the reader
this before the reading starts, so it is a rule and not a trap.
Consequence stated so nobody has to rediscover it: an EMPTY or text file written
here fails post-read verification. That is intended — an empty render is not a
render, and a text file here is either a mistake or a smuggle, and the tool should
say so rather than skip it.
_forbidden_derivation: The 21 tracked paths naming the paper at BASE_HEAD cbce3016, enumerated by:
plus claim_registry_current.md and working_model_current.md — which do NOT name the
paper and are excluded anyway, because they carry what the laboratory already concluded
about it; plus controlled_benchmark_ab.md, which describes this experiment and names
the paper. Governance candidates are excluded from the surface wholesale, so listing
each of them here would be noise.

_note: The paper's identifiers must not appear in anything that is not the paper. The packet
is exempt because it IS the paper; the instructions are exempt because a reader must
be told which PMID it is reading. Everything else scans to zero, or the surface is
not blind. Verified 2026-08-18 on all nine non-instruction text files: 0 hits each.
Structural enumeration of what the paper CONTAINS. Rules are declared here so the
population is a function of (spec, source) and can be re-derived by anyone.
REVISION 2 — the whole block was rebuilt after Mirror finding B-1. What changed and why:
(1) NO FIXED CAPTION WINDOW. A caption now runs to the NEXT MATCH OF ITS OWN RULE,
or to the end of the segment. The 3600-character window ran 925 characters past
Figure 2's caption into Figure 3's and reported TWELVE panels for a caption that
prints SIX. A fixed integer bounds the wrong axis: the axis a caption window
fails on is whether it respects the next label.
(2) METHODS ARE DERIVED, NOT LISTED. The twenty hand-enumerated headings were a
list, not a rule (R-6), and were short by four. Sections are now selected by
TYPOGRAPHY — the face and size the paper sets a heading in — inside a region
bounded by two declared markers. Recovered: Ca2+ Imaging, WWOX and MYC
expression invivo, ChIP-seq analysis (all three named by Mirror), and
'Library preparation and Single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) (10x Chromium)', a
heading that WRAPS across two lines and that a line-bounded rule cannot see.
(3) RESULTS HEADINGS ARE ENUMERATED, not promised. Protocol §8.1 named them and no
rule existed. They are typographically distinct in this source, so the promise
is kept rather than narrowed.
(4) EVERY PACKET SOURCE IS ACCOUNTED FOR. File011 (resource table) and File012
(uncropped blots) yielded zero units and were therefore unmeasurable; both are
now enumerated. File008 yields none and says so, under declared_empty_sources.
The command REFUSES a spec that leaves a packet source unclassified.
notes: PANEL EXTRACTION IS FROM CAPTIONS, and the caption is what the paper printed.
(1) Supplementary Figure 1 yields A-I, K, L, M — no J. The caption labels (G) twice and
never labels J; the enumeration reports the paper, not a repair of it.
(2) Figure 6 labels its panels [A(i)], [A(ii)], [B(i)]… and the range (C-D). Ranges are
expanded; a single-letter pattern alone reported A,B,E and would have made the
denominator short by two, which flatters both readers' coverage.
(3) The main text carries no numbered Table — main_table is 0 by measurement, not by
(4) Every figure label is reprinted in a trailing size listing ('Figure 2 / 140x90 mm').
The FIRST occurrence is the caption and is the one kept; the repeat is skipped, and it
also serves as the bound of Figure 6's caption, which is the last one in the text.
(5) File012 keys its uncropped blots to supplementary figure PANELS, not to figures.
Supplementary Fig. 1J spans two pages; it is ONE source-data unit, met twice.
(6) File012 prints its keys inconsistently — 'Supplementary Fig. 5B' with a space and
'Supplementary Fig.6F' without. Labels are reported AS PRINTED, not normalized: the
enumeration reports the paper, and a tidied label is a label no reader can grep for.
This population fixes WHAT the paper contains. It does not rank units by importance:
which of them matter is what the two readings and the adjudication are for.

declared_empty_sources.reason: Author contributions only — one page, a CRediT-style role list naming no figure, table, method or datum. It carries no evidence unit, so no coverage over it is claimed and none is measurable. It stays in the packet because both readers must see the same packet; it is excluded from the denominator because there is nothing in it to cover.

_note: The article sets its section headings in Aptos Display: 20.27 for a top-level
section, 15.77 for a subsection. Body text is Times New Roman 12. Both rules below
are bounded by top-level markers, so neither can reach into the section after it.
The supplement sets a Methods heading in Times New Roman Bold 15.96; the section
title 'Materials and methods' is 18.00 and the cover page is 21.00 / 12.00, so
neither is selected. 'References' is bold at the SAME 15.96 as a heading — size
alone cannot exclude it, which is why it bounds the scope by name.
The tools-and-reagents list is one supplementary table. Its resource categories are
merged full-width rows, centred at x≈291.4; the four column-header cells (Resource,
Source, Catalog, Number) sit in their columns at x≈112, 302, 467 and are excluded by
that geometry, not by being named. page_from 2 skips the cover page.
Uncropped immunoblots, one page per blot, each keyed to the supplementary figure
panel it is the source data for. The label is the key; spacing after 'Fig.' varies
in the source ('Supplementary Fig. 5B' and 'Supplementary Fig.6F' both occur), so
the pattern tolerates it and the label is normalized to a single space.
